I read this book several years ago, when it first came out and my son’s high school made it recommended reading for its students, something that I’m 100% sure would not happen today. It told the story (ostensibly a biography) of a kid from difficult circumstances in Appalachia who made it to Yale Law School. That’s before Vance decided to get involved in politics, after failing in venture capital. Looking at it today, he so inflates his resume that it makes me wonder weather anything in the book is factual. For example, he constantly talks about being a Marine in Iraq, as if he were dodging bullets in foxholes. In fact, he was refining his ability to spin stories to the press, working as an assistant in the Marine press office, far from the front lines. He briefly worked in “private equity” and formed his own private equity fund at one point, but the performance of his fund was dismal. He did benefit from it by being introduced to some billionaire investors who have used him to advance their own self-interests. It’s true that he was a Senator from Ohio, elected with the help of those same billionaires, but only for a few months before being selected to run for VP, whereupon he began worshipping the same man who he had spoken negatively repeatedly previously. He hardly graced the Senate floor, let alone learned anything from teh experience. He apparently did go to Yale; I have two Ivy League degrees and I can assure you that an Ivy League degree is far from endorsement of one’s intelligence or, even more so, integrity.

Rarely have we had a less qualified or experienced Vice President. Yet, the actuarial tables tell us that a 78-year old man of average health has about a 25% chance of dying within the next four years, so Vance has at least a 25% chance of being our next President.

Don’t waste your time or money on this book. Harry Potter is better fiction.
